limits: Linux benchmark host (4 vCPU Xeon, 15.7 GiB); not the Mac. The Mac command is provided, not run.

Equal resources: every campaign ran alone on the same three CPUs (1-3). The fast path's prefix helpers and replay threads use CPUs that the accepted path and PR30 leave idle; single-CPU optimizer-only comparisons are reported separately.

Host drift: the host's speed changed during the night. The same accepted work took 1.3 to 1.4x as long in the evening of 26 Oct as at night (B 4,214.9 s against B2 3,230.4 s; C 3,241.7 s against C2 2,481.1 s; accepted baselines 876 s against 636 to 652 s), and fast-path work took up to 1.3x as long in the morning as at 04:00 to 05:00 UTC (RE266 2,174.4 s and RD266b 2,130.6 s against RD266 1,839.2 s; RE267 646.6 s against RD267 503.6 s; m6-REH 1.00 to 1.16x m4-RDH per batch). Ratios within a pair measured at the same time are stable; the headline brackets the accepted campaign between two fast-path campaigns.

The accepted path cannot complete training batch 266 from 629 on this host: its update is stopped at the 3,540 s budget and rolled back, after 83 of 125 optimizer steps in the evening (m1-B, batch 3,523 s) and after 116 at night (m6-B, batch 3,519.6 s, the same games). Ratios against it are lower bounds; the night run's own step rate puts the complete batch at about 3,790 s (an extrapolation over the last 9 of 125 steps). The evening estimate of 4,600 to 4,900 s measured the slower evening host and is not used.
The projection uses the measured batches from the 629 parent (sequences 266 onward); later batches depend on how long the policy's games become. It is a scale, not a forecast.

Projections are comparable only between variants measured on the same sequences (each variant's projection lists its distinct_sequences): batches 266 and 267 alone average less than the six batches 266 to 271 (799 s against 902 s in m4-RDH), so a projection from 266 and 267 only is biased low.

The engine delivers some notices asynchronously, so a game can differ in event order between runs with the same seeds (one of twelve games in two accepted runs; m6-RBH batch 266 game 4). Such batches are not comparable and are not used as evidence of exactness either way.
Three host restarts (about 23:15, 23:49 and 03:25 UTC) interrupted m1-F, two PR30 runs, m6-RBH (after two admitted batches) and RBN267; every lost job was rerun or reported as lost.
Campaign summaries and lossless compression of raw episodes run between campaigns, briefly on CPU 0, while the optimizer-only queue runs there.
Fork safety of the overlapped verification and prefix helpers with Torch loaded on macOS is unverified; the macOS default uses neither (Mac letters O and H test them).
The shared_graph_encodings experiment is numerically different (reordered gradient summation) and reported separately; it is never a default.

m6-REH's batches 268 to 270 each have one game of four that differs from m4-RDH's (asynchronous event order, with the same decision counts); they are timed but not used as evidence of exactness either way.

(``--games 5000 --eval-every 100``: 1,250 training updates; eight evaluation
games before the first update, after every 100 updates and at the end, 26 evaluation batches of one seat):
    wall = cold start + 1,250 x (mean measured training batch) + 26 x (mean measured evaluation batch)
from batches of this host that start at the 629 parent. Later batches depend on how long the policy's games
become; nothing here predicts that, so the projection is a scale, not a forecast.
